THIS WEEK IN LOCAL GOVERNMENT

Marathon County approved a $55 million highway facility and Wausau's Public Health & Safety Committee voted to pull the plug on Flock license plate reader cameras, while local governments from Kronenwetter to Weston worked through 2027 budget proposals.

  • Marathon County authorized roughly $54.98 million in Phase 4 construction of a new highway facility, with a board-added requirement to develop a divestment strategy for the existing West Street site.
  • Wausau's Public Health & Safety Committee voted unanimously to recommend striking Flock camera contract funding and directing police to immediately cease using the surveillance system.
  • Wausau Finance Committee cut $50,000 in Flock camera funding, $45,000 in alley paving, $150,000 for a city administrator position, and $20,000 in trail planning from the proposed 2027 budget.
  • Wausau Plan Commission forwarded Yawkey Park's landmark designation to City Council and approved rezoning 909 South 60th Avenue from medium to heavy industrial.
  • Kronenwetter's Plan Commission postponed action on a conditional use permit for a non-metallic mine at 1320 Kowalski Road, citing thin attendance, and will schedule a special meeting.
  • Weston's Board of Trustees approved a 10-year loan at 4.95% for the new Mountain Bay Metro Police headquarters and narrowly passed (4-3) a policy stating written public comments will not be read aloud.

Coming up: Tuesday brings a busy night at the county and city level, with the Marathon County Board meeting at 7 p.m. and Wausau's Common Council convening at 6:30 p.m. — expect Council action on the Flock camera recommendations. Wednesday, DC Everest holds its annual meeting and budget hearing at 6 p.m.
